title: Alphabet had its worst day ever and Intel lost 29%
dek: Big tech's cash burn finally hit the stocks. The Nasdaq fell 2.0% on the week as oil climbed to a six-month high and the Fed held.
summary: Alphabet's worst day ever, Intel down 29%, and the cash burn story behind both. Plus earnings, the Fed holding, oil at a six-month high, and the week ahead.
keyNumbersNote: Oct 30 close, change since Oct 23 close

briefs.headline: Alphabet's worst day ever
briefs.body: Alphabet fell 12.6% on Thursday, its biggest one-day drop on record, erasing about $500 billion in value. It missed on revenue and earnings for the first time in nearly four years, and free cash flow came in at negative $9.07 billion against about negative $2.7 billion expected.

briefs.headline: Intel crashes, chips follow
briefs.body: Intel lost 28.6% on Friday, its worst day since the 1970s, after guiding fourth-quarter revenue to $15 billion to $16 billion against $17.1 billion expected. AMD fell 10.9%, Qualcomm 11.1% and Nvidia 4.2%, and the chip index dropped 7.2%.

briefs.headline: Cash burn is the story
briefs.body: Amazon became the third hyperscaler, after Alphabet and Meta, to report negative free cash flow. The S&P 500 fell 1.8% on Friday, its worst day since June, and posted a third straight losing week, while the Russell 2000 rose 1.3%.

briefs.headline: Fed holds, two want a hike
briefs.body: The Fed kept rates at 3.75% to 4.00% in a 10 to 2 vote, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a quarter-point hike. "Inflation remains elevated," the statement said.

briefs.headline: Economy runs hot, yields slip
briefs.body: Third-quarter GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate, up from 2.2%. The 10-year yield touched 5.05% on Fed day but ended the week at 4.94%, down 6 bp, and the 2-year fell 13 bp to 4.56%.

briefs.headline: Oil at a six-month high
briefs.body: Brent settled at $117.64 on Friday and WTI at $104.12, both up about 2% on the day, after a tanker was mined in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent rose 13.6% in October and WTI 15.2%.

earningsLead: Cash flow beat the headlines. Microsoft held up, Alphabet and Intel were crushed.

earnings.line: Azure grew 48% to $33.17B, above estimates, and it guided 49% to 50% next quarter. Stock -0.2%.
Revenue $127.58B vs $128.22B expected, EPS $2.67 vs $3.02. Kept 2026 capex at $195B to $205B. Stock -12.6%.
Missed on revenue and EPS; AWS grew 39%, its fastest in nearly five years. Stock -1.4%.
EPS beat at $0.52 vs $0.40, but a weak fourth-quarter guide. Stock -28.6%.
Revenue $24.40B vs $22.61B; raised 2026 sales guide to $91B to $92B. Stock +6.6%.
EPS beat at $7.20, but it kept its 2026 sales outlook below forecasts. Stock -9.3%.

items: ISM manufacturing. Apple and Palantir report after the close.
Midterm elections. JOLTS job openings. AMD reports after the close.
ADP employment and ISM services. Qualcomm, Uber and McDonald's report.
October jobs report at 8:30 AM. Forecast: 55,000 jobs, unemployment 4.2%.
